response:
Diagnosis. The archive now shows a clear split. Signals whose short leg is "weak firm raising capital" reliably produce strong FMB slopes (-2.6 to -4.1) but their FF5 alphas collapse to zero or flip positive (IssuanceAgainstDepletedRetainedEarnings +1.6%, EquityTilt +4.3% t 3.3, TwoWayEquityChurn +11% with Sharpe -1.18). The reason is not statistical noise: the extreme deciles of those sorts are small, unprofitable, high-asset-growth firms whose raw underperformance is already spanned by SMB, RMW and CMA, so what survives as "alpha" is a loading residual, not a mechanism. By contrast the single design that delivered *joint* evidence is BuybackFundingSource (fmb 2.90, alpha +3.5%, t 3.32, Sharpe 0.38): a one-sided distribution intensity multiplied by a **signed funding-source gate** built from a second financing variable. Its long and short legs are both distributing firms — similar size and profitability profiles — differing only in *where the cash came from*, which is precisely why FF5 cannot span the spread. This generation therefore consolidates the funding-source mechanism across other financing actions and margins, and spends two slots on mechanisms designed to escape the FF5-absorption trap on the negative side rather than repeating it.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: TotalPayoutFundingSource
EXPRESSION: MUL(RATIO(ADD(prstkc, dvc), at), SUB(RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Any distribution to shareholders — dividends as well as repurchases — is credible only if the firm is simultaneously generating the cash internally rather than replacing it in the capital markets; firms that distribute with one hand while raising equity or debt with the other are recycling investor capital and their payout carries no valuation information.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This isolates two specific design choices relative to the archive's best signal: broadening the distribution leg from repurchases to total payout (which repairs the zero-inflated prstkc base the critic flagged and should raise coverage and portfolio stability) and broadening the external-funding side of the gate from debt issuance to all outside capital. If the funding-source contrast rather than the buyback event is what FF5 cannot span, this should retain the alpha with a better-populated long leg.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: DeleveragingFundingSource
EXPRESSION: MUL(RATIO(dltr, at), SUB(RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), RANK(RATIO(sstk, at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Debt retirement means opposite things depending on its source: repaying maturing debt out of operating cash flow signals a business that has outgrown its leverage, whereas retiring debt with proceeds from selling equity is creditor-driven balance-sheet repair that transfers value from shareholders to bondholders.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: CredibleDeleveraging failed on alpha (t 0.89) because its non-negative gate contrasted levered against unlevered firms — groups FF5 separates on its own — whereas here both legs are firms actively repaying debt and the contrast is purely the funding source, the feature that made BuybackFundingSource survive FF5. It extends the winning mechanism to a completely different financing action, so a positive result would establish funding-source credibility as a general principle rather than a buyback artifact.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: FiveYearSelfFundingShare
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(oancf, 5), ADD(TS_SUM(oancf, 5), TS_SUM(ADD(sstk, dltis), 5))), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: The share of a firm's five-year cash inflows that came from its own operations rather than from capital markets is a slow-moving measure of financial self-sufficiency; markets underprice the durability of self-funded business models and overprice firms whose growth history is an accumulation of outside capital.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is a ratio-form interaction in which quality is the numerator and financing the complement, so it is not decomposable into a quality term plus a financing term, and its multi-year accumulation makes portfolio membership stable rather than driven by one lumpy issuance year. It also tests the reverse framing of the archive's negative-side failures: instead of shorting extreme issuers (whom FF5 already spans), it goes long the self-funded population, a group that spans size and industry rather than concentrating in microcaps.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: AccrualIllusionIssuanceAmongProfitableFirms
EXPRESSION: MUL(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at), MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), INDICATOR(MA(RATIO(ib, at), 3), 0)))
HYPOTHESIS: Capital raising is most mispriced when the issuer looks healthy on the income statement but its earnings are accrual-driven; such firms are neither distressed nor obviously low quality, so investors extrapolate reported profits and fund the raise, and the subsequent accrual reversal is what the market misses.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Every negative-sign archive signal gated issuance on weakness (cash burn, depleted retained earnings, low ROA), and each one saw its alpha absorbed or reversed by FF5 because those gates select the small-distressed corner that SMB, RMW and CMA already span; restricting the sort to firms with positive multi-year earnings deliberately removes that corner and asks whether the mispricing survives among ostensibly profitable issuers. The accrual gate is a quality-of-earnings measure rather than a profitability level, so the resulting spread should have far more balanced factor exposures.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: DebtRolloverChurnUnderIlliquidity
EXPRESSION: MUL(MIN(RATIO(dltis, at), RATIO(dltr, at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Simultaneous large long-term borrowing and repayment is refinancing rather than net funding, and refinancing is a benign treasury operation for firms with a comfortable working-capital buffer but a symptom of maturity-wall pressure for firms whose current assets barely cover current liabilities.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The MIN of gross issuance and gross retirement measures rollover volume, a quantity that all net-debt-flow signals in the archive mechanically cancel, and the gate uses balance-sheet liquidity rather than profitability or cash flow, so it conditions on a quality dimension FF5 does not represent. This tests whether refinancing pressure — as opposed to net capital raising — is the part of the debt channel that carries return information.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: DividendIncreaseFundingSource
EXPRESSION: MUL(DELTA(RATIO(dvc, at), 1), SUB(RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: A rising dividend is a commitment that only self-funding firms can keep; when a firm raises its dividend in the same year it is tapping outside capital, the increase is a signal-jamming gesture that predicts later reversal, while a dividend increase paid out of strong internal cash flow is genuine information about sustainable earnings power.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This applies the winning funding-source gate to the change margin rather than the level, which makes both tails active — internally funded raisers at the top, externally funded raisers and internally funded cutters at the bottom — and avoids the non-payer mass that deadened earlier dividend-level signals. Paired with Signal 1 it separates whether funding-source credibility operates on the stock of distributions or on the news in changing them.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---CRITIQUE TotalPayoutFundingSource---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: This is essentially the archive's best signal (BuybackFundingSource) with both legs mechanically broadened — payout to prstkc+dvc (already tested as PayoutCredibilityGate) and financing to sstk+dltis — so it reads as a cosmetic union of two archived constructs rather than a new mechanism, and the smooth, persistent dividend level will likely dominate the payout scale and pull the sort toward the known payout-yield anomaly.

---CRITIQUE DeleveragingFundingSource---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Extending the funding-source contrast to gross debt retirement is a genuinely different financing action with a coherent nonnegative-scale × signed-gate construction, though the gate alone (high operating cash flow minus high equity issuance) is close to a known profitability-plus-issuance composite, so much of any resulting alpha may be a rescaled version of well-documented effects.

---CRITIQUE FiveYearSelfFundingShare---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The ratio is non-monotone and unstable whenever five-year operating cash flow is negative or close to offsetting cumulative issuance (denominator can approach zero or turn negative, flipping the sign for the most distressed firms that the signal is supposed to short), and once winsorized it is largely a monotone repackaging of the well-known external-financing/net-issuance anomaly scaled by cash-flow profitability.

---CRITIQUE AccrualIllusionIssuanceAmongProfitableFirms---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The mechanism — issuance conditioned on accrual quality — is the same one already tested as DilutionQualityGate (with the sign merely reversed by using ib−oancf instead of oancf−ib), and because every factor in the product is nonnegative and the indicator zeroes out all unprofitable firms, the long leg becomes a large tied mass of zeros rather than an economically identified group.

---CRITIQUE DebtRolloverChurnUnderIlliquidity---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: Rollover volume via MIN(issuance, retirement) is a quantity that all net-debt-flow signals mechanically cancel and the working-capital gate is a balance-sheet liquidity dimension absent from FF5, making this a substantively new test, though it inherits the structural fragility seen in the archived MIN-based churn signal and the working-capital gate will pick up strong industry/business-model tilts.

---CRITIQUE DividendIncreaseFundingSource---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Multiplying a signed dividend change by a signed funding-source gate makes the sign economically incoherent in one quadrant: firms cutting dividends while heavily tapping outside capital (negative × negative) land in the long leg, and internally funded cutters land in the short leg, which directly contradicts the stated credibility mechanism.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: BuybackAtOwnCashFlowPeak
EXPRESSION: MUL(RATIO(prstkc, at), SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(oancf, at), 5), RANK(RATIO(dltis, at))))
HYPOTHESIS: A repurchase is credible when the firm is buying stock at a moment when its own cash generation is unusually strong by its own standards and it is not borrowing to do so; the same repurchase executed when internal cash flow is at a personal low and long-term debt is being drawn is balance-sheet engineering.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: Rather than broadening the archive's best signal, this isolates the single design question its result leaves open — whether the alpha comes from the cross-sectional profitability rank (which is RMW-like and could be a factor artifact) or from the genuine funding-source contrast — by replacing the cross-sectional cash-flow rank with the firm's own five-year cash-flow position. If the alpha survives with a within-firm internal-funding measure, the mechanism is timing and funding credibility rather than a profitability tilt, which is the more valuable finding for the remaining generations.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: MultiYearSelfFundingGap
EXPRESSION: SUB(TS_SUM(RATIO(oancf, at), 5), TS_SUM(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at), 5))
HYPOTHESIS: Over a full business cycle a firm either pays for itself or is paid for by the capital markets; the cumulative gap between five years of internally generated operating cash and five years of outside capital absorbed identifies durable self-funding franchises at one end and serial market-dependents at the other, a distinction investors underweight because it is invisible in any single year.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: Expressing self-funding as a difference of asset-scaled cumulative flows rather than as a share removes the non-monotonicity the critic identified — there is no denominator that can approach zero or change sign, so the most cash-negative serial issuers now sit unambiguously at the bottom instead of wrapping around to the top. The five-year accumulation also makes portfolio membership slow-moving, which addresses the instability that has plagued the archive's one-year issuance sorts whose alphas evaporated under FF5.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: ExpansionFundingSource
EXPRESSION: MUL(MUL(GROWTH(at, 1), INDICATOR(GROWTH(at, 1), 0)), SUB(RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Growth is not intrinsically good or bad; what matters is who paid for it. Expansion financed out of operating cash flow reflects a business reinvesting its own surplus, while identical expansion financed by outside capital reflects management appetite unconstrained by internal performance and is systematically overpriced at the time of the raise.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This moves the funding-source principle that produced the archive's only joint FMB-and-alpha result from the payout side to the investment side, a genuinely different economic decision, and it is not the accruals-times-issuance construction the critic identified as a re-test of DilutionQualityGate. The indicator restricts the action leg to firms that actually expanded, so both tails are growing firms distinguished only by funding source, while shrinking firms sit at zero in the middle rather than forming a tied mass in either leg.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: DividendHikeFundingSource
EXPRESSION: MUL(MUL(DELTA(RATIO(dvc, at), 1), INDICATOR(DELTA(RATIO(dvc, at), 1), 0)), SUB(RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Only firms generating internal cash can keep a raised dividend; a dividend increase declared in the same year the firm is tapping equity or debt markets is a signal-jamming gesture that is later reversed, whereas an increase paid from strong operating cash flow conveys sustainable earnings power.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: Taking the positive part of the dividend change removes the incoherent quadrant the critic identified — externally funded cutters can no longer be pushed into the long leg, and internally funded cutters can no longer be shorted — so every firm in either tail is a dividend raiser and the sort is purely about how the raise was financed. Paired with the payout-level evidence already in the archive, it tests whether funding-source credibility operates on the news in a payout decision rather than on its level.
